data.change_summary: Reworked the chloride emergency regression so it now compares a chloride-rich water change against both a matched water-change control and a salt-treated branch with chloride protection disabled, using validated carbonate inputs instead of the invalid copied DIC/alkalinity pair. I also kept the current per-stage molt-timer contract aligned with the schema-guarded save migration by updating coverage to drive explicit stage timers and guard against runtime backfill from `inter_molt_timer_days`, then patched adjacent denitrification/save-load initializer fallout so the affected core and scenario test suites compile again.
outstanding_risks: A broader `cargo test -p tank_core` sweep still fails in `crates/tank_core/tests/thermal_reproduction_penalty.rs`; that regression appears unrelated to the molt/chloride amendments and was not widened into this stage.

steps.description: Rebuilt the salt-treatment emergency scenario around cloned post-crash states, validated source-water carbonate inputs, and matched control/no-protection branches so the test now guards chloride-specific mortality relief instead of generic water-change improvement.

Kept the runtime/save-load molt-timer contract centered on per-stage timers by updating shrimp population coverage to use explicit stage timers and adding a regression that zero stage timers are not backfilled from the legacy population timer during runtime.

Fixed compile fallout from newer denitrification and save-state fields by completing the nitrogen-cycle output initializer, seeding `denitrifier_activity_index` in the save-load fixture, and wiring default denitrification parameters through scenario materialization where presets do not yet provide them.
Ran targeted shrimp/save-load regressions plus `tank_data`, `tank_scenarios`, and a broader `tank_core` pass to verify the amendments and capture remaining unrelated failures.
